newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's biggest tanker ablaze after blast.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's biggest tanker ablaze after blast.

text.p: Turkey's biggest oil tanker was ablaze in Istanbul's Tuzla dockyard late on Thursday after an explosion.
"The fire is continuing and we won't be able to put it out until all the fuel inside is burned up," Tuzla governor Erdogan Gurbuz told Reuters. "But thank goodness there are no dead."
Officials at Tuzla said 18 people were injured in the fire, most of them firemen. Two of them, hurt in the original blast, were in serious condition. One of the injured was Chines, television said.
The fire appeared to be dying out at around 2000 GMT.
Witnesses saw firemen walking into ambulances, their garments burned to rags and their hair singed. Some were dragged into ambulances.
Turkish television showed a man ablaze on deck, his clothes all burned off. He later managed to put out the fire. Three other firemen had jumped into the sea to safety, private ATV television said.
Gurbuz said the fire had been confined to the TPAO tanker. ATV said two dry cargo ships had also caught fire, but these fires had been extinguished.
He said the dockyard workers had already left the ship at the end of their shift just as the explosions began.

Officials said the TPAO, at 159,982 deadweight tonnes, was Turkey's biggest oil tanker. The tanker, which was built in 1977 and is owned by the Istanbul company Ditas, was in the yard for repairs and carried no oil.
Witnesses saw the ship engulfed in flames, which flared up with every explosion. Clouds of black smoke could be seen even in the darkness of the night.
"Work is continuing from sea and land to put out the fire. We have set up a crisis centre for the accident," Gurcan Dagdas, the state minister responsible for marine affairs, told Kanal D.
Dagdas said the ship had been brought into the dockyard eight days ago.
The power of the blast shattered windows of buildings in settlements some distance from the dockyards. There were no houses near the dockyard, officials said.
Gurbuz said explosions in the gas depot were responsible for the fire, but the reason for the blasts was unclear.
